newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS RALLY FOR GAME ONE WIN OVER SABRES.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS RALLY FOR GAME ONE WIN OVER SABRES.

text.p: Shjon Podein stuffed in a wraparound goal with 48 seconds left in regulation as the Philadelphia Flyers rallied for a 5-3 win over the Buffalo Sabres in the opener of their Eastern Conference semifinal series on Saturday.

Rod Brind'Amour tallied twice for the Flyers, tying the game midway through the third period and sealing the victory on an empty netter with six seconds left as Philadelphia battled back from a 3-1 deficit with four unanswered goals.
An apparent go-ahead tally by Buffalo's Rob Ray with 8:06 to play was disallowed by referee Don Koharski, who ruled that Wayne Primeau was in the crease.

Replays showed Primeau was checked into the crease by Chris Therien and briefly held there by Flyers goalie Garth Snow. He was trying to exit when Ray scored, but Koharski stood firm in his decision and the score remained 3-3.
The game appeared headed for overtime when Podein gained control of a loose puck behind the Buffalo net and shoved it around the right goalpost, through Shields's pads.
"I'm a happy camper now to have done this," Podein said. "I can't believe I scored a sudden death goal like this."
Game Two of the best-of-seven series is Monday in Buffalo.
The Flyers were returning from a week of inactivity following their swift five-game dismissal of Pittsburgh in the opening round and appeared a bit rusty.

The Sabres, coming off an emotional seventh-game overtime win over Ottawa, took advantage and jumped out to a 2-0 lead with goals 42 seconds apart by Michal Grosek and Brad May early in the second period.

Philadelphia got one back when Dan Kordic beat Shields at 11:23 of the second, driving home a rebound of Dainius Zubrus's shot. But Donald Audette beat Snow on a power play to restore the two-goal lead at 17:26.

Audette's goal came 21 seconds after play resumed following a stoppage of some 15 minutes due to a skirmish deep in the Philadelphia zone that saw the two goaltenders trading punches. Both goalies received fighting majors and minors for leaving the crease, but Snow picked up an extra roughing penalty, giving Buffalo the power play.
Depite the Buffalo goal, the scuffle was just what the physical Flyers needed, according to Brind'Amour.
"The melee helped us," he said. "It jump-started us. We needed a kick in the pants. We were sluggish after the layoff."

Still, the Sabres appeared about to take a 3-1 lead into the lockerroom when Paul Coffey picked up an errant clearing attempt and fed Mikael Renberg, who put the puck past Shields with just half a second left on the clock.

"We got a big goal at the end of the second period by Renberg and that propelled us for the third," said Flyers forward Dale Hawerchuk, who set up Brind'Amour's equaliser at 10:00 of the final period.

"He (Hawerchuk) feathered a neat pass to me. I had a breakaway and punched it into the five hole," said Brind'Amour, referring to the space between the Buffalo goalie's legs. "The puck is going in for me."
Brind'Amour notched his fifth post-season goal when he intercepted a clearing pass and scored into an empty net.
Shields, playing again for the first injured and then suspended Dominik Hasek, made 42 saves. Snow faced 32 shots and stopped 29.
"We played very well and should have won. I'm disappointed," lamented Buffalo coach Ted Nolan.
"Philadelphia will only play better. This was the night we had a chance to take them."
